risks.title: Customs Tariffs
risks.score_rationale: Customs tariffs imposed by the U.S. government could increase costs of construction materials and other goods, impacting operating results and planned capital expenditures.

risks.title: Rate Regulation
risks.score_rationale: CPUC decisions directly impact authorized revenues and rates of return on investment. Rejection of certain decoupling mechanisms (full WRAM) increases earnings volatility.

risks.title: Consumption Volatility
risks.score_rationale: Volatility in water and electricity consumption can impact results, particularly with the transition to a less protective M-WRAM (Monterey-style).

risks.title: Regulatory Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly dependent on regulatory approvals for cost recovery, capital investments, and investor returns.

risks.title: Supply Contract Risks
risks.score_rationale: Contracts with purchased water and power suppliers may carry price and availability risks.

risks.title: Supply Chain Management Risks
risks.score_rationale: Supply chain management for construction materials and equipment may involve risks related to delays and costs.

risks.title: Cybersecurity Risks
risks.score_rationale: Cybersecurity risks could impact critical operational systems for water and electricity distribution.

ai_positioning.summary: AWR does not mention artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies in its 10-K filing for the 2025 fiscal year. No references to AI are present in the provided excerpts.
